chief_complaint: right lower quadrant abdominal pain and fever
hpi_details: 45M presents with 12 hours of periumbilical pain that has now migrated to the right lower quadrant, accompanied by nausea, one episode of vomiting, and subjective fever.
expectations: wants pain relief and a CT scan

investigation_events.title: Urgent appendicitis results
investigation_events.availability_message: The urgent appendicitis results are now available; IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics, and surgical consultation should not be delayed.

results.test: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
results.value: Dilated appendix measuring 10 mm with periappendiceal fat stranding; no abscess, perforation, or free air

core_concepts: Classic presentation is periumbilical pain migrating to RLQ.
Diagnosis is often confirmed with CT scan in adults.
common_misconceptions: Assuming all RLQ pain is appendicitis.
dangerous_errors: Discharging patient with classic migrating pain without imaging or observation.
management_principles: NPO, IV fluids, analgesia, antibiotics, surgery consultation.

source_refs.title: SAGES & ACS Evidence-Based Surgical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 45M with migrating RLQ pain, nausea, and fever.
reference_soap.objective: T 38.2C, RLQ tenderness with guarding (McBurney's point).
reference_soap.plan: CT abdomen/pelvis, NPO, IV fluids, surgery consult.

teaching.one_liner: Classic acute appendicitis presenting with migrating RLQ pain, fever, and nausea.

must_ask.say: Did the pain start around your belly button and then move to your lower right side?
When exactly did the pain start, and how has it changed since then?
Have you lost your appetite, felt nauseated, or vomited?
Have you had any fever or chills?
Does moving, coughing, or pressing on your belly make the pain worse?

history.answer: My lower right belly hurts really badly, and I have a fever.
It started about twelve hours ago as a dull stomachache, and it has steadily gotten worse through the night.
It began around my belly button, but after several hours it shifted down to my lower right belly.
No, it stays right in my lower right stomach and does not travel to my back, shoulder, or groin.
It started as a dull cramp, but now it feels like a constant, sharp ache.
When it first started it was about a three, but now it is a steady seven out of ten.
Any movement, walking, or coughing makes it hurt much more. Lying completely still with my legs curled up helps a little bit.
No, I have never had abdominal pain like this before.
I felt very nauseous this morning and vomited once. It was just clear fluid and stomach bile, with no blood in it.
My last bowel movement was yesterday morning and it was normal. I have not passed any gas in several hours, but I do not have diarrhea.
No, there has been no blood in my stool and my bowel movements have not looked black.
Yes, I have been feeling quite feverish and hot since early this morning, and I had mild chills.
No, my eyes and skin have not turned yellow, my urine is not dark, and my stools are normal brown.
No, I do not have any burning when I pee, no blood in my urine, and I am not peeing more often than usual.
No, I have not felt dizzy, lightheaded, or like I was going to faint.
No, I have no chest pain, tightness, or shortness of breath.
I had a normal home dinner with my family yesterday evening, nothing greasy or unusual, and I did not drink any alcohol.
No, I have not taken any pain relievers or aspirin because I was afraid they might irritate my stomach.
No, I have never had an irregular heartbeat, atrial fibrillation, or any blood vessel disorders.
I was wondering if this could be appendicitis because the pain moved to my lower right side.
I am really worried that my appendix might burst and that I might need emergency surgery.
I am hoping you can give me something for this severe pain and do a CT scan to see what is happening.
I do not have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I have never had any surgeries and I have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any daily prescription medications, over-the-counter pills, or herbal supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I have never smoked in my life.
I only drink occasionally, maybe one or two beers a month at social gatherings, and nothing this past week.
I work in an office as an IT specialist and live with my wife and two children.
There is no family history of serious gastrointestinal illnesses or early surgical problems.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 125/80 mmHg, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 16 breaths per minute, body temperature 38.2 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on ambient air.
The patient appears acutely uncomfortable and lies still on the examination table with hips and knees slightly flexed to reduce abdominal tension.
The abdomen is flat and symmetric with no distension, visible pulsations, or surgical scars.
Bowel sounds are hypoactive throughout all four quadrants, and no vascular bruits are audible.
Marked focal tenderness and voluntary guarding are present in the right lower quadrant, while the remaining quadrants are soft and non-tender without diffuse rigidity.
Rebound tenderness is sharply positive in the right lower quadrant and absent in all other quadrants.
Point tenderness is localized at McBurney point, with a positive Rovsing sign and pain elicited on right psoas stretching.
Murphy sign is negative, with no tenderness or inspiratory arrest during deep palpation of the right upper quadrant.
No costovertebral angle tenderness is elicited on percussion bilaterally.
No rectal masses, hemorrhoids, or frank blood are present, though mild tenderness is noted high on the right rectal wall.
